title: Buy Now, Pay Later and Bankruptcy: What You Need to Know
summary: Law-firm blog post explains how BNPL debt is treated in Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcy and what raises fraud red flags.

assertions.quote: Buy now, pay later debt might feel different than a credit card bill—but under bankruptcy law, it's treated the same way.
The creditor could argue that you never intended to repay the debt and used the BNPL service fraudulently.

verdicts.note: Standard bankruptcy fraud doctrine (non-dischargeability for debts incurred without intent to repay) applies to BNPL the same way it applies to credit cards.

assertions.quote: While not all BNPL lenders report to credit bureaus, more of them are starting to.
Miss a payment, and late fees or collection actions kick in fast.

verdicts.note: Documented across providers: Afterpay/Klarna/Zip all charge late fees or pause accounts on missed payments despite advertising zero interest.

assertions.quote: Too many small balances can add up.
